# coder_template_outputs (Data Source)

This development data source is deprecated. Use [`coder_foundation`](foundation.md)
for combined Foundation metadata and outputs. The compatibility data source retains
its template-based ID and existing attributes; it is not an alias for Foundation
identity. Both require the companion development provider and matching Coder server.

It reads the immutable shared resource outputs snapshot supplied by Coder to a
per-workspace build, not live Terraform state or an API endpoint. A Foundation owns
its shared resources independently of attached templates.

## Example usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    coder = {
      source = "coder/coder"
    }
  }
}

provider "coder" {}

# Deprecated compatibility data source. Prefer coder_foundation for new templates.
# Coder supplies an immutable snapshot with Terraform types and sensitivity.
data "coder_template_outputs" "shared" {}

locals {
  template_outputs = data.coder_template_outputs.shared.outputs

  # Template import can run before shared resource outputs exist. Pick a
  # fallback appropriate for the consuming resource, rather than indexing directly.
  subnet_ids = try(local.template_outputs.network.subnet_ids, [])
}

output "subnet_ids" {
  value     = local.subnet_ids
  sensitive = true
}

output "template_resource_revision_id" {
  value = data.coder_template_outputs.shared.revision_id
}
```

## Environment contract

| Variable | Attribute | Missing or empty fallback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CODER_TEMPLATE_OUTPUTS` | `outputs` | `{}` |
| `CODER_FOUNDATION_OUTPUT_METADATA` | `outputs` types and sensitivity | Legacy JSON type inference |
| `CODER_TEMPLATE_RESOURCE_REVISION_ID` | `revision_id` | Empty string |
| `CODER_FOUNDATION_ID` | `foundation_id` | Empty string |
| `CODER_WORKSPACE_TEMPLATE_ID` | `id` | `import` |

When output metadata is supplied, the values and metadata follow the exact-type
[Foundation contract](foundation.md#environment-contract). Sensitive outputs are
not filtered. The entire `outputs` attribute is marked sensitive if any root
output is sensitive. Sensitive data is still stored in Terraform state.

For compatibility with older development servers, absent or empty metadata enables
JSON type inference: arrays become tuples and objects become objects, so original
list, set, and map types cannot be recovered. This legacy path does not mark the
attribute sensitive and must only receive snapshots from servers that excluded
sensitive outputs. New integrations must always provide metadata for nonempty
snapshots. Numbers retain Terraform precision in both paths.

Use `try` for optional output keys and empty snapshots during import. Nonempty
Foundation and revision IDs must be UUIDs. `revision_id` identifies the legacy
shared resource revision, not the producing run exposed as
`coder_foundation.snapshot_id`. Neither data source selects versions or enforces
compatibility policy. Coder supplies a pinned snapshot; Terraform determines whether
required outputs are available.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `foundation_id` (String) UUID of the Foundation supplying the snapshot, or an empty string when unavailable. This metadata does not select a Foundation or revision.
- `id` (String) ID of the template, or `import` when unavailable during template import.
- `outputs` (Dynamic) Object containing shared resource output values. Exact Terraform types and sensitivity are preserved when output metadata is supplied. The entire attribute is sensitive if any root output is sensitive. Defaults to an empty object during template import.
- `revision_id` (String) UUID of the shared resource revision supplying the snapshot, or an empty string when unavailable during template import.
